Redeploy source store to .claude/ via deploy-headless.sh
Confirm task-lookup-lib.sh present in deployed tree
Run full gate set (cycle-plan, triage-classify, cycle-postflight, check-task-references)
Verify no file under .claude/** was hand-edited
End-to-end smoke test on real completed and archived tasks
objectives.note: Live smoke test against this repo's real ~1MB specs/archive/state.json surfaced a real defect in Phase 5's classifier archive read (jq --argjson archived over Linux's 128KiB MAX_ARG_STRLEN, exit 126, silent fallback). Fixed in-phase: both call sites in orchestrate-triage-classify.sh now write the flattened archive to a mktemp temp file and read it back via --slurpfile instead of embedding it as a command-line argument. Added mutation-checked Case 5 fixture coverage (both engines) in test-orchestrate-triage-classify.sh. Re-ran the full gate set and the live smoke test after the fix; all green.

approaches_tried.approach: Run cycle-plan.sh directly against the real repo's specs/state.json in-place
approaches_tried.reason: PROJECT_ROOT resolves from the invoking script's own path (SCRIPT_DIR, 2 levels up), independent of --state-file, so a copy-only smoke test would still write real dispatch files into the real specs/189_.../ and specs/archive/137_.../ directories. Switched to a fully isolated /tmp root with a symlinked .claude/ and copied specs/ tree instead.

deviations.description: orchestrate-triage-classify.sh's two jq --argjson archived call sites (state-lookup and verdict composition), added in Phase 5
deviations.reason: Live smoke test against this repo's real archive/state.json (1,009,723 bytes) reproduced 'jq: Argument list too long' (exit 126) on every classifier invocation -- the flattened archive exceeds Linux's 128KiB per-argument MAX_ARG_STRLEN when passed via --argjson. Fixed by writing the flattened archive to a mktemp temp file and reading it back via --slurpfile at both call sites, matching the stdin-piping pattern task_lookup_entry already uses safely. Added mutation-checked Case 5 fixture coverage.
